title: Consolidate token parsers and upgrade transitive crypto dependencies to mitigate CVE regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We have recurring security findings from dependency scans where transitive crypto and SSO-related packages (OpenSSL bindings, JWT helper libs, and legacy SAML adapters) are pulled in by multiple small token-parsing utilities across services. Several small, uncoordinated updates have introduced subtle behavioral differences (clock skew handling, claim normalization) that created flaky auth failures and one regression flagged by internal QA. Goals: 1) Consolidate token parsing and verification into a single shared library used by auth-adapters; 2) Upgrade direct and transitive crypto-related dependencies (OpenSSL/BoringSSL wrappers, jose/jwt libraries, saml adapters) to vetted versions that address known CVEs; 3) Add compatibility shims and tests to preserve runtime behavior and avoid user-visible regressions; 4) Produce a roll-out plan for staged deploys and a backout path. Acceptance criteria: - Single shared token-parser package published and consumed by services requiring JWT/OAuth/SAML token handling. - All transitive crypto deps upgraded to versions with CVE fixes (listing in linked doc). - Regression test suite covers claim normalization, time-window verification, unusual clock skew scenarios, and canonicalization of SAML NameID formats. - No increase in SSO errors in canary window (observability dashboard comparison). - Security sign-off from security@redwood and dependency-scan passes on CI. Out-of-scope: Rewriting core SAML authentication flows and replacing the IdP fleet. Implementation notes: - Create token-parser as a semver-stable package with clear compatibility guarantees. - Use feature flags to enable new parsers per-service during rollout. - Introduce a small shim library for legacy adapters to avoid mass rewrites. - Coordinate with infra on BoringSSL/OpenSSL ABI compatibility on dedicated pools to avoid runtime linker issues.
comments: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting — agreed to prioritize consolidation before bulk upgrades to limit behavioral drift. Action: Marco to draft package API by 2025-02-14.

2025-02-14: API draft posted in Confluence (link below). Design: token-parser exposes verify(), parseClaims(), and normalizeSamlNameId(). Decision: preserve existing claim mapping by default and provide opt-in strict mode.
2025-02-20: Dependency audit complete. Found 12 transitive paths pulling in vulnerable OpenSSL wrappers in two services. Proposed pinned versions and backport patches listed in the audit doc.
2025-02-24: First PR created: token-parser initial implementation and adapters for auth-service and sessions-service. Tests: unit + integration harness for clock skew. PR: GH#4567.
2025-02-27: QA report: minor regression in sessions-service where a legacy token with missing 'iss' was previously accepted. Added compatibility shim for iss-legacy tokens and updated test vectors.
2025-03-01: Security reviewed PRs and approved pinned deps. Security requested one additional test for simultaneous key-rotation scenarios; added to test plan.

2025-03-02: Canary deploy started for auth-service in us-east-1 with feature flag controlled rollout at 10% traffic. Monitoring dashboards created for SSO error rate, latency, and token verification failure categories.
change_log: 2025-02-20: Performed full SBOM and transitive dependency mapping. Identified vulnerable paths and listed recommended pins.
2025-02-24: Implemented token-parser v0.1.0 with adapters for two services. Added claim normalization tests and clock-skew harness.
2025-02-27: Added compatibility shim to accept legacy tokens without 'iss' when feature-flag enabled.
2025-03-01: Upgraded jose-jwt to 4.8.1 and patched internal OpenSSL wrapper to 1.1.1k-backport. Ran full CI smoke tests.
2025-03-02: Canary rollout started (10% auth-service traffic). Monitoring configured; awaiting 72h observation window.
notes: Risk: Upgrading transitive crypto libs can surface ABI and behavior incompatibilities. Mitigation: run binary smoke tests on dedicated GPU pools with packaging that mirrors production runtime. Rollback: feature-flag disable plus immediate revert PR ready. Coordination: inform platform-ops about the upgraded native bindings; they will pre-pull updated native packages to dedicated nodes.
